P1.evidence: P1a partial — the application is acknowledged but nothing is read back: 'I saw your application that you sent to us, but I want to get in more detail about your situation.' P1b partial — two of four frame elements ('what you're trying to achieve with your fitness health wise too. And see how can we potentially help you with that'). P1c miss — no frame agreement sought. P1d hit — well framed and open: 'could you walk me through like what's been going on? Like what's the main thing you're looking to fix right now?' The rep also checked the prospect was not driving, which was appropriate given he was parked at the roadside.

P2.evidence: The most thorough baseline in the batch — six clean hits — which is exactly what makes the downstream failure so stark. P2d hit and best-in-batch: asked directly ('do you have like any injuries or anything that limits your movements?'), then pushed past the first answer twice ('anything that's maybe not an injury, but something that's like small aches and pains here and there' and 'No lower back pain, stiffness, nothing?'), and established duration ('And that happened in what timeframe?'). That sequence surfaced an ankle reconstruction, bilateral knee problems and a cervical fusion. P2b hit — asked exactly as scripted: 'how about your work? Is it more like you move around or is it more sedentary?', though the rep never asked what the work actually IS, which left occupation unknown for a 68-year-old hospital worker. P2e hit — current training fully mapped. P2g hit and genuinely investigative — he refused the surface answer ('Not always to help. That's the main thing. Like, what actually are you consuming?') and then quantified the eating out at three to four nights of seven. P2h hit — sleep asked, then the wakings probed for cause, which opened the retirement stress. P2a miss — age was volunteered in the first sentence; height and weight were never asked at all, on a call whose stated goals are losing belly fat and rebuilding muscle mass. P2c miss and material — no health conditions, no medications, no blood pressure, no cardiac or hereditary history, for a 68-year-old. P2f and P2i partial.

P3.evidence: Surface goals captured, deep why never attempted. P3b hit — 'why kettlebells? What made you reach out to us?' produced the goal set: 'I'm looking for improved mobility, flexibility, and things, and maybe build muscle, lose body fat.' P3a and P3c partial. Then nothing. P3d miss — the bridge question, 'outside of the physical, what's actually driving this right now?', was never asked. P3e miss. P3f miss — a wife and a physical-therapist daughter are both mentioned and neither is ever connected to the goal. P3g miss and the largest single omission on this call — no drive through to longevity, independence, family or identity, on the oldest prospect in the batch, a 68-year-old losing muscle mass who is the most natural longevity conversation in the entire corpus. P3h miss. Worst of all, the rep walked directly past the strongest available bridge: the prospect volunteered 'I think a lot about retiring, Andrew, to be honest with you... making sure I have financial wherewithal to be able to retire comfortably. And I do not have that right now, so I can't retire.' Retirement he cannot yet afford, and a body losing the capacity to enjoy it when it comes, is the entire emotional case for this purchase. The rep's next line was 'Have you ever tried kettlebells before?'

P4.evidence: P4a hit — a full history surfaced: half marathons, sports, personal trainers, five to six years of martial arts, home yoga and calisthenics, Instagram and Facebook programmes. P4b hit — the outcome established as a five-year decline. P4c hit and asked twice, correctly: 'Why did you stop, uh, doing all those things?' and later, when the timeframe turned out to be five years rather than two, 'Why? You've been so active.' P4d and P4e partial — the rep accepted an unexamined answer. The prospect said 'Life, you know, life. Honestly, I don't know. It's just kind of gotten... I've felt more tired lately. My work has been more pressured lately' and the rep moved to sleep instead of pressing on the 'I don't know'. That is precisely the moment the script exists for. P4f miss — the information-isn't-the-problem frame never delivered, and it was well suited here to a prospect who follows free Instagram programmes and knows what a healthy meal is.

P5.evidence: Not run at all. Fourth call in this batch with no consequence frame, and the most costly instance of the four. A 68-year-old who has watched five years of muscle loss and can describe exactly what it looks like was never asked what another two or five years of the same produces, never asked whether he was willing to settle for it, and never asked to draw a line. The closest the rep came was a challenge question at 00:11:09 — 'because you haven't been doing a lot for last years, how do you think this time is going to be different when you're so busy?' — which is a good question, but it tests commitment rather than establishing cost, and it belongs to P6. With no consequence established, the $6,000 twelve minutes later had nothing to be weighed against, which is the likeliest reason a prospect who had just said 'Yes, sir. I am' walked away thirty minutes later asking to postpone by a month.

P6.evidence: P6b hit and cleanly answered: 'if we can figure out all the logistical details, are you fully committed to showing up and doing the work?' / 'Yes, sir. I am, Andrew.' P6c hit — the yes was taken before the price was named. P6a partial — the scripted belief question about structure and the right person in his corner was not asked in form, but the rep set up an explicit fit test at the start of the presentation ('you let me know if it actually fits your life... if this is something that check all the boxes for you') and collected a substantial answer at the end, which the prospect gave in unusual detail: 'What really excites me is the fact that I will have interaction with Trevor... I think it's one thing that sets this program above anything that I've looked at so far.' Sequencing note: the pillars were again presented before the commitment check.

P11.evidence: P11a miss, and this is a genuine miss rather than an unreachable phase, because the prospect asked to pay and the rep declined. 'I will go to my office and I'll sit down and I will work out payments if you send me the link' was answered with 'Oh, we need to go over the call because I need to onboard you properly, get you on a call with Trevor and so on.' The reasoning is defensible — the rep wanted the onboarding done live rather than left to drift, and the prospect was in a parked car — but the outcome is measurable: the ten-minute gap he created was long enough for the prospect to look at his finances and return asking to postpone the whole thing by a month. P11b, P11c and P11d are N/A because none were reachable once payment was deferred.

objection_plays.detail: Soft money resistance appeared and was never isolated. 'I'm going to have to look at that, but okay. I understood. How do you take payments?' contains both a hesitation and a buying question, and the rep answered only the second. No 'finances aside, nothing else keeping you from 100%?', no 'you're not in a SHOULD I place, you're in a HOW place', and not one of the six financial-picture questions. One scripted move ran in substance — breaking it up — but only as third-party financing over twelve months, subject to credit score, with no rate, provider or total repayable stated. Most consequentially, the interest-free in-house instalment plan was not offered here. Thirty minutes later the same rep offered exactly that plan to the same prospect and closed him in ninety seconds, and the prospect's own account of this call was 'you didn't mention installments, you just said put it on a credit card and pay the credit card off.'

'I'm going to have to look at that' is a think-about-it in substance and no OA move ran. No belief-check at the point of hesitation, no 'so what's actually coming up that's preventing you from getting started?', no 'thinking isn't the problem, deciding is'. The rep treated the line as an acknowledgement rather than as an objection and moved to logistics.
No spouse consult raised on this call, though a wife is mentioned in the context of eating out.
No timing objection on this call. It surfaced thirty minutes later on the continuation, where the prospect opened by asking to postpone by a month.
No fear or doubt about the modality — he had used kettlebells with a previous personal trainer and was actively enthusiastic about the form-feedback mechanism.

SCRIPT GAP AND THE MOST SERIOUS INSTANCE IN THE BATCH — clinical fit. The prospect disclosed, in direct response to a well-asked question, an ankle reconstruction limiting dorsiflexion, bilateral knee problems preventing squatting, and a cervical fusion of the neck. There is no scripted path for any of this. The rep did not ask what the restrictions mean in practice, did not ask whether a clinician would clear ballistic loaded kettlebell work, did not make the sale contingent on clearance, and did not suggest involving the prospect's own daughter, a physical therapist who has already assessed his movement pattern. He said 'That's great. That's great.' and moved to nutrition. The playbook already records having no clinical-fit play; this call shows the cost of that gap at its sharpest, because the screening question WAS asked and the answer changed nothing.

SCRIPT GAP — no play for a prospect who is ready to buy but cannot transact from where he is. The prospect verbally agreed and asked for a link. The rep had no sanctioned option other than to refuse and rebook, because the process requires payment and onboarding to happen live on the same call. There is no deposit-now-onboard-later path, no send-link-and-stay-on-the-line path, and no hold mechanism. The rule cost momentum here and very nearly cost the deal.

SCRIPT GAP — a disclosed retirement funding shortfall. 'Making sure I have financial wherewithal to be able to retire comfortably. And I do not have that right now, so I can't retire.' This is simultaneously the strongest emotional lever available (a retirement he is working toward and a body that may not be able to enjoy it) and the clearest possible signal of constrained discretionary spend. The playbook offers no guidance for either reading, and the rep used neither — the disclosure was acknowledged and dropped.

notes: Excellent information gathering, almost none of it used. The baseline is the best in the batch and the past-attempts work is solid, but P3 collapsed after the surface goals, P5 was skipped entirely, and the two most valuable disclosures on the call were both heard and discarded. The first is clinical and urgent: a cervical fusion, bilateral knee problems and a restricted ankle were volunteered in answer to a direct question, met with 'That's great', and followed by a six-month loaded kettlebell offer with no clearance sought and a physical therapist in the family who was never mentioned. The second is commercial: 'I can't retire' was said fourteen minutes before a $6,000 ask and never connected to it, in either direction. Add the decision to refuse a payment link that the prospect asked for, and this call produced a prospect who said 'Yes, sir. I am' and then, thirty minutes later, asked to postpone by a month. Coaching priorities in order: seek clinical clearance whenever a surgical history is disclosed, run P5 before the price, and mine the retirement thread rather than stepping over it.
